en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Qays ibn 'Ubad, who said: I was in Medina among people, including some of the Companions of the Prophet (pbuh). A man arrived on whose face was a trace of reverence. Some of the people said, "This is a man from the people of Paradise; this is a man from the people of Paradise." He prayed two rak'ahs, keeping them brief, then he left. I followed him, and he entered his residence, and I entered. We talked, and when he became at ease, I said to him, "When you entered earlier, a man said such-and-such." He said, "Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah)! It is not appropriate for anyone to say what he does not know, and I will tell you why that is. I saw a vision during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and related it to him: I saw myself in a garden—he mentioned its vastness, its grass, and its greenness—and in the middle of the garden was an iron pillar whose bottom was in the earth and whose top was in the sky. At its top was a handhold. It was said to me, 'Climb it.' I said to him, 'I cannot.' Then a minsaf came to me"—Ibn 'Awn said: a minsaf is a servant—"and he took hold of my clothes from behind me"—he described that he lifted him from behind him with his hand—"so I climbed until I was at the top of the pillar, and I grasped the handhold. It was said to me, 'Hold firmly.' I woke up and it was indeed in my hand. I related it to the Prophet (pbuh), and he said: 'That garden is Islam, that pillar is the pillar of Islam, that handhold is the most trustworthy handhold, and you will remain upon Islam until you die.'" He said: And the man was 'Abdullah ibn Salam.

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to us, 'Arim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet of Allah (pbuh) confided a secret to me, and I never told anyone about it afterwards. Umm Sulaym indeed asked me about it, but I did not tell her of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Bahz narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit informed us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) came upon me while I was playing with the boys. He said: He greeted us with salam and sent me on an errand, so I was late in returning to my mother. When I arrived, she said, "What kept you?" I said, "The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) sent me on an errand." She said, "What was his errand?" I said, "It is a secret." She said, "Do not disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) to anyone." Anas said: "By Allah, if I were to tell it to anyone, I would have told you, O Thabit."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ja'far—meaning Ibn Sulayman—narrated to us, from al-Ja'd Abu 'Uthman, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) passed by, and my mother Umm Sulaym heard his voice and said, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Here is Unays." So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) made three supplications for me, of which I have seen two in this world, and I hope for the third in the Hereafter.

Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi narrated to me, 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, 'Ikrimah narrated to us, Ishaq narrated to us, Anas narrated to us, who said: My mother, Umm Anas, brought me to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), having dressed me with half of her head-covering as a waist-wrapper and covered me with the other half. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Unays, my son; I have brought him to you so that he may serve you, so supplicate to Allah for him." He said, "O Allah, increase his wealth and his children." Anas said: By Allah, my wealth is indeed abundant, and my children and my children's children count to about one hundred today.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (pbuh) entered upon us, and there was no one but me, my mother, and Umm Haram, my maternal aunt. My mother said, "O Messenger of Allah, your little servant, supplicate to Allah for him." He said: So he supplicated for every good for me, and the last of what he supplicated for me was that he said: "O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in it."
Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd: I heard Anas ibn Malik say the like of that.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: I heard Anas saying: Umm Sulaym said, "O Messenger of Allah, your servant Anas..." and he mentioned similarly.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas, from Umm Sulaym, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, your servant Anas, supplicate to Allah for him." So he said: "O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in what You have given him."

Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Musa ibn Khalid, son-in-law of al-Firyabi, informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I used to stay overnight in the mosque and had no family. Then I saw in a dream as if I were taken to a well... and he mentioned from the Prophet (pbuh) with the meaning of the hadith of al-Zuhri from Salim from his father.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and the wording is 'Abd's—they said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: During the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), whenever a person saw a dream, he would relate it to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). So I wished that I would see a dream that I could relate to the Prophet (pbuh). He said: And I was a young, unmarried youth, and I used to sleep in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). Then I saw in sleep as if two angels took me and went with me to the Fire, and behold, it was cased like the casing of a well, and behold, it had two horns like the two horns of a well, and behold, inside it were people I recognized. So I began saying, "I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire! I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire! I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire!" He said: Then an angel met them both and said to me, "Do not fear." So I related it to Hafsah, and Hafsah related it to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). The Prophet (pbuh) said: "What an excellent man 'Abdullah is, if only he would pray during the night." Salim said: After that, 'Abdullah would not sleep at night except a little.

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki, Khalaf ibn Hisham, and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari all narrated to us from Hammad ibn Zayd—Abu al-Rabi' said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us—Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I saw in a dream as if there were in my hand a piece of fine silk brocade, and there was no place in Paradise that I wished for except that it flew to it. He said: So I related it to Hafsah, and Hafsah related it to the Prophet (pbuh), and the Prophet (pbuh) said: "I see 'Abdullah as a righteous man."

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr both narrated to us—they said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Warqa' ibn 'Umar al-Yashkuri narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid narrating from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (pbuh) entered the privy, so I placed ablution water for him. When he came out, he said, "Who placed this?" In the narration of Zuhayr: they said; and in the narration of Abu Bakr: I said, "Ibn 'Abbas." He said: "O Allah, grant him deep understanding of the religion."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Marwan—meaning al-Fazari—narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Abu Usamah narrated to us—all of them from Isma'il, with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of Marwan he said: "Then Jarir's bearer of glad tidings, Abu Artah Husayn ibn Rabi'ah, came conveying glad tidings to the Prophet (pbuh)."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to me: "O Jarir, will you not relieve me of Dhu al-Khalasah?"—a house belonging to Khath'am that was called the Ka'bah of Yemen. He said: So I set out with one hundred and fifty horsemen. I could not sit firmly on horses, so I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), and he struck his hand upon my chest and said: "O Allah, keep him firm and make him a guide who is guided." He said: So he went and burned it down with fire. Then Jarir sent a man from among us with the kunyah Abu Artah to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) to convey the glad tidings. He came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and said to him: "I have not come to you until we left it looking like a mangy camel." Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) invoked blessings upon the horses of Ahmas and its men five times.

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to me, Khalid informed us, from Bayan, from Qays, from Jarir, who said: In the pre-Islamic days of ignorance there was a house called Dhu al-Khalasah, and it was also called the Yemeni Ka'bah and the Sham Ka'bah. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Will you not relieve me of Dhu al-Khalasah and the Yemeni and Sham Ka'bah?" So I set out to it with one hundred and fifty from Ahmas, and we demolished it and killed whomever we found at it. Then I came to him and informed him. He said: So he supplicated for us and for Ahmas.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Qays, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) never screened himself from me since I embraced Islam, nor did he look at me without smiling in my face. Ibn Numayr added in his narration from Ibn Idris: "And I complained to him that I could not sit firmly on horses, so he struck his hand upon my chest and said: 'O Allah, keep him firm and make him a guide who is guided.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abdullah informed us, from Bayan, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah; (H) and 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to me, Khalid narrated to us, from Bayan, who said: I heard Qays ibn Abi Hazim saying: Jarir ibn 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) never screened himself from me since I embraced Islam, nor did he see me without smiling.

Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah al-Sami and Muhammad ibn Hatim both narrated to me—and their narrations were close in context, with the wording being Ibn Hatim's—they said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Jamrah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When news of the Prophet's (pbuh) mission reached Abu Dharr in Mecca, he said to his brother: "Ride to this valley and find out for me about this man who claims that news comes to him from heaven, listen to his words, and then come back to me." So the other set out until he reached Mecca, listened to his words, and then returned to Abu Dharr and said: "I saw him enjoining noble character traits, and speech that is not poetry." Abu Dharr said: "You have not satisfied me regarding what I wanted." So he packed provisions and took a small waterskin of his containing water until he reached Mecca. He came to the mosque and sought the Prophet (pbuh), while he did not know him and disliked asking about him, until it overtook him—meaning night. So he lay down, and 'Ali saw him and recognized that he was a stranger. When he saw him, he followed him, but neither of them asked the other about anything until morning came. Then he carried his small waterskin and his provisions to the mosque, and spent that day without seeing the Prophet (pbuh) until evening came. Then he returned to his sleeping place, and 'Ali passed by him and said: "Has the time not come for the man to know his dwelling place?" So he made him stand up and took him with him, and neither of them asked the other about anything until the third day arrived, when he did the same. 'Ali made him stand up with him, then said to him: "Will you not tell me what brought you to this land?" He said: "If you give me a covenant and a pledge that you will guide me, I will do so." 'Ali did so, and he informed him. 'Ali said: "Indeed, it is true, and he is the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). So when morning comes, follow me; if I see anything that I fear for you, I will stand as if I am passing water. If I proceed, then follow me until you enter where I enter." He did so, and set out following his tracks until he entered upon the Prophet (pbuh), and Abu Dharr entered with him. He listened to his words and embraced Islam on the spot. The Prophet (pbuh) said to him: "Return to your people and inform them until my command reaches you." He said: "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I shall shout it aloud among them!" So he went out until he reached the mosque, and cried out at the top of his voice: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah!" The people rose against him and beat him until they knocked him down. Then al-'Abbas came, threw himself over him, and said: "Woe to you! Do you not know that he is from Ghifar, and that your merchants' route to Sham passes by them?" So he rescued him from them. Then he returned the next day and did the same, and they rose against him and beat him, and al-'Abbas threw himself over him and rescued him.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, who said: Abu Dharr said: "O son of my brother, I used to pray two years before the mission of the Prophet (pbuh)." He said: I asked, "So where did you face?" He said: "Wherever Allah directed me." And he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, and in the hadith he said: "So the two of them went for arbitration to a man from among the soothsayers." He said: "My brother Unays kept praising him until he overcame him." He said: "So we took his herd of livestock and added it to our herd." And he also said in his hadith: He said: Then the Prophet (pbuh) came and circumambulated the House and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam. He said: So I came to him, and I was the first person to greet him with the greeting of Islam. He said: I said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "And upon you be peace; who are you?" And in his hadith also: He said, "How long have you been here?" He said: I said, "For fifteen." And in it: Abu Bakr said, "Grant me the honor of hosting him tonight."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, with this chain of narration; and he added after his statement: "I said: So look after my affairs until I go and see." He said: "Yes, and be cautious of the people of Mecca, for they have become hateful and hostile toward him."
